nodes.label: cached
nodes.rationale: Wraps a handler with response caching keyed by a user-supplied key(req); a hit serves the stored response without invoking the handler. Defaults to caching only status 200 so a transient 500 never sticks around, and does not auto-invalidate on writes - staleness is bounded by ttlMs, with short TTLs or a direct cache.delete of the prefixed key as the two stronger-consistency patterns.

nodes.label: Cache key composition
nodes.rationale: key(req) is the entire cache-key contract. req.path is the pathname only, never the query, so an endpoint whose response varies by a query parameter has to fold it in or every page shares one entry and page 2 is served page 1. Omitting the user from the key on an authenticated endpoint leaks one user's response to all of them.

nodes.label: Per-process single-flight
nodes.rationale: On a miss the wrapper runs the handler once per process and other concurrent requests for the same key await that single result via an in-process single-flight map. It is not cluster-wide: with N pods the handler can run up to N times concurrently. Stale-while-revalidate is not built in.

nodes.label: Response cache is the key-minting side
nodes.rationale: key(request) almost always derives from something the client controls, so a caller who varies it mints a new entry per request. Harmless here - the LRU bound is exactly what stops the response cache growing without limit - but not harmless in an instance shared with rateLimit or idempotent, where eviction picks the least-recently-used entry with no idea it holds a rate-limit counter or a record stopping a double payment.
